releaseApproval.reviewer: Release deployment explicitly authorized by the user in the project conversation; automated implementation evidence recorded locally and required in Linux CI
evidence: The user requested deploying the extensible update fix. v1.3.7 is the first immutable legacy updater bridge; future releases retain its verified five-member compatibility envelope while current workers choose complete manifest-driven packages.

This change preserves the previously approved encrypted object, key derivation, AAD, metadata, SQLite, backup, and client mutation contracts. It adds release package format 1 and a controlled application-file installation boundary.

Go regression and race checks, portable installation/upgrade checks, variable-file package tests, twenty-resource deployment, removal of obsolete managed files, full directory/database rollback, administrator-file preservation, and interrupted directory-switch recovery passed locally. Both Linux architectures packaged successfully and all four candidate archive digests and manifests were verified.

Publication requires successful exact-commit main CI on Ubuntu, including project checks, all-package race tests and Linux cross-builds. An actual systemd two-stage legacy-to-future update rehearsal was not executed locally; that limitation remains recorded for target VPS rollout.

sqlite.migrationPolicy: forward only; after a schema-changing migration, restore the matching pre-migration database and binary before rollback

clientMutationProtocol.acceptance: exact match only; reject missing, older, and future versions before reading mutation bodies

evolutionPolicy: Unknown payload versions and unknown fields remain fail-closed.
The listed optional fields and their absent-value meanings are part of the current schema contract.
Adding or redefining a payload field requires a new payload schema version; it must not silently expand an older strict reader.
A change that makes a stale client unsafe for mutations increments the client mutation protocol version in Go and TypeScript.
Key derivation or AAD meaning changes use their own crypto version; they do not reuse a payload schema number.
SQLite schema migration, backup container format, encrypted object envelope, and browser payload schema are independent version dimensions.
